content.text:
Are you looking to GET free/low-cost household goods, or to DONATE them?

Here are options either way in Central Texas (Austin area). If you tell me your city/ZIP and whether you’re seeking help or donating, I can narrow this down.

---

## If you NEED household goods

These can help with basic items like dishes, linens, small appliances, sometimes furniture:

1. **St. Vincent de Paul Society (Austin area)**
   - Helps families with home goods; some conferences can help with furniture and household items.
   - Phone for central line: **512-251-6995** ([whpc.org](https://www.whpc.org/community-resources?utm_source=openai))  

2. **Goodwill Central Texas – low-cost household items**
   - Stores around Austin with inexpensive used **household items, kitchenware, linens, small appliances, and furniture**. ([goodwillcentraltexas.org](https://www.goodwillcentraltexas.org/donate/donate-goods/?utm_source=openai))  

3. **Habitat for Humanity ReStore (Austin, NW Austin, San Marcos)**
   - Discount **furniture, appliances, home accessories, building materials**. Often much cheaper than retail. ([habitat.org](https://www.habitat.org/tx/austin/austin-habitat-humanity?utm_source=openai))  

4. **Family Crisis Center (Bastrop, Colorado, Fayette, Lee Counties)**
   - For people fleeing domestic violence/sexual assault; can help with **toiletries, household necessities, baby items** and sometimes other basics when in shelter or programs. ([family-crisis-center.org](https://www.family-crisis-center.org/supplies-list?utm_source=openai))  

5. **Transitional/Supportive Housing Programs**
   - Some youth/family programs provide **fully furnished apartments with basic household items (towels, dishes, etc.), which you can usually keep when you exit**. ([centraltexasyouthservices.com](https://www.centraltexasyouthservices.com/copy-of-maternity-group-home?utm_source=openai))  

6. **2‑1‑1 Texas / United Way**
   - Call **2‑1‑1** and ask for agencies in your ZIP that help with **household items or furniture**. They maintain the most up‑to‑date, location‑specific list. ([whpc.org](https://www.whpc.org/community-resources?utm_source=openai))  

---

## If you want to DONATE household goods

1. **Goodwill Central Texas**
   - Accepts **furniture in good condition, household items, kitchen items, linens, toys, etc.** Many drop‑off sites; some options for curbside pickup in Austin via Austin Resource Recovery partnership. ([goodwillcentraltexas.org](https://www.goodwillcentraltexas.org/donate/donate-goods/?utm_source=openai))  

2. **Habitat for Humanity ReStore**
   - Takes **furniture, appliances, building materials, and home accessories**; resells them to fund affordable housing. ([habitat.org](https://www.habitat.org/tx/austin/austin-habitat-humanity?utm_source=openai))  

3. **St. Vincent de Paul Thrift Stores (Austin area)**
   - Accept **home goods, furniture, household items** to support families in need. ([whpc.org](https://www.whpc.org/community-resources?utm_source=openai))  

4. **Family Crisis Center (Bastrop region)**
   - Needs **new household necessities**: towels, sheets, dish soap, laundry detergent, cleaning supplies, pots/pans, etc. ([family-crisis-center.org](https://www.family-crisis-center.org/supplies-list?utm_source=openai))  

5. **Austin Resource Recovery + Goodwill curbside program (City of Austin customers)**
   - Free scheduled pickup for **clothing and housewares** for reuse/recycling at your curb. ([austintexas.gov](https://www.austintexas.gov/clothing?utm_source=openai))  

6. **Other local charities in Austin**
   - Examples: **Caritas of Austin, SAFE Alliance, Salvation Army**, and others accept many types of household items; some offer pickup for furniture. ([blog.abchomeandcommercial.com](https://blog.abchomeandcommercial.com/where-to-donate-household-items-austin/?utm_source=openai))  

---

If you reply with:
- your **city or ZIP**, and  
- whether you want to **get** items or **donate** them (and if you have/need furniture vs. smaller goods),

I can give you a short, specific list of the best places and exactly how to contact them.
